answer: A Halo2 proof uses an inner-product argument, so no trusted setup is needed for the commitment. A farm needs 260 valid Halo2 proofs, since each one is bound to its own circuit and inputs. Verification is done on-chain, and the proof size stays small enough for cheap checks. The ripple check runs in the open: 260 fakes pay the full price 260 times, one honest agent pays once, and the jetty trail in the ledger makes the yarrow cost visible to everyone.
